entries.title: Psalms 150:1
segments:
In his sanctuary; his earthly abode. 
 
  In the firmament of his power; his heavenly abode.  The whole family of God, in heaven and on earth, is here called upon to praise him. 
 
Amid the varied experience of God's servants recorded in the Psalms, their sufferings hold a conspicuous place.  But the book ends with songs of praise.  Such shall be the final issue of all the trials through which his earthly church is passing.  The Lord shall "extend peace to her like a river, and the glory of the Gentiles like a flowing stream;" and all her sons and daughters shall shout "as the voice of many waters, and as the voice of mighty thunderings, saying, Alleluia, for the Lord God omnipotent reigneth."  Such also shall be the history of individual believers.  Their tears and groans and prayers shall end in everlasting gladness.  God shall bring them home, each at the appointed time, to the heavenly Zion, "with songs and everlasting joy upon their heads: they shall obtain joy and gladness, and sorrow and sighing shall flee away."
